# ADR-057 — Present-state reconciliation of the decision log (Checkpoint 8.0)

**Status:** Locked

<!-- Decision text below is verbatim from the pre-split docs/DECISIONS.md table row (2026-09-16). Do not edit a Locked decision without explicit owner approval. -->

**Present-state reconciliation of the decision log (Checkpoint 8.0, 2026-09-02).** This ADR corrects factual claims that earlier ADRs make about the CURRENT system and that are no longer (or were never) true. **No decision is reversed and no historical rationale is rewritten** — the original cells are left intact and each carries a pointer here, because editing a Locked cell's text would itself be a change to a Locked decision. Every correction below was verified first-hand against the repository at `533601c`. **1. ADR-047's sweep clause is false in both halves.** It states that *"only operational metadata (`health_sync_runs`, expired OAuth states) is swept"*. Neither is swept. `sweepExpiredOAuthStates` (`apps/api/src/services/health-connection.ts:173`) and `sweepExpiredMailOAuthStates` (`apps/api/src/services/mail-connection.ts:179`) are defined and exported with **zero production callers** — the only reference to either outside its own definition is one health unit test. `health_sync_runs` has no DELETE anywhere outside test teardown. OAuth state rows are *consumed* (`consumed_at` set by UPDATE), never deleted, so `health_oauth_states` and `mail_oauth_states` grow monotonically. Conversely the one automatic deletion that DOES run in production is unnamed by the clause: the hourly orphan-audio file sweep (`apps/worker/src/jobs/sweep-orphan-audio.ts`), which deletes user audio blobs rather than operational metadata. **ADR-047's load-bearing prohibition is unaffected and remains Locked: no health measurement is ever automatically deleted, expired or pruned.** Wiring the two sweeps is deferred and is not Checkpoint 8.0 work. **2. ADR-054's mail prune does not exist.** It calls a bounded prune of `mail_messages` and `mail_sync_runs` *"permitted and required"* with a window that *"must be explicit, configurable, and recorded in `docs/STATUS.md`"*. There is no prune job, no queue, no cron, and no retention key in either `env.ts`; no window is configured anywhere; and nothing is recorded. The code is self-aware of the gap (`apps/worker/src/mail/persist.ts:182`). The DECISION stands — a prune is still permitted and still required — but it is **deferred, unimplemented, and its window is unset**, and choosing that window is an owner decision because ADR-024 makes deletion irreversible. **3. ADR-054's claim that email is "the first attacker-authored input to reach the AI layer" is false as a statement about capability, and true only as a statement about occurrence.** Externally-authored calendar text has had a shipped, unfiltered path into the Daily Brief prompt since Checkpoint 5.5, roughly a week before ADR-054 was written: `event.summary`, `description` and `location` arrive verbatim from Google (`packages/calendar-providers/src/translate.ts:389-391`) and CalDAV, are written unbounded into `events.title/description/location` (`packages/db/src/schema/events.ts:25-27`, plain `text`, **no Zod `.max()` and no truncation at write** — precisely the gap ADR-054 claims mail avoids), and reach the prompt through `read-models/event-range.ts`, `read-models/today.ts` and `brief/collect-input.ts`. Two mitigations exist and two do not: `description` never reaches the model, and `title`/`location` ARE truncated at the prompt boundary (120 and 80 characters) — but the Brief lane has **no output filter** (`sanitizeDigestText` exists only under `apps/worker/src/mail/digest/`), and `apps/api/src/brief/prompt.ts:28` still asserts *"the data you receive does not contain any of these"*, which is the exact false premise ADR-054 identified and required be rewritten for the digest. **The path has never been exercised in production**: `events` is 0 and the only sync-enabled calendar is a dedicated empty test calendar, so no third-party text has traversed it. Capability, not occurrence — and the correction is recorded because conflating the two in either direction would be wrong. Backporting the filter and bounding event text at write is Checkpoint 8.1 work and is a **precondition for enabling a real calendar**. **4. ADR-055's dedupe claim holds for monitoring and fails for both integration producers.** It says alert dedupe keys are *"incident-scoped"*. Of the five `category: "alert"` producers, the three monitoring ones are correctly incident-scoped. The two integration producers are not: `calendar-needs-reauth:<connectionId>` (`apps/worker/src/jobs/calendar-refresh-token.ts:144`) carries **no discriminator at all** and is the known-burned example ADR-055 was written against; and — **newly identified at Checkpoint 8.0** — `health-sync-alert:<connectionId>:<reason>` (`apps/worker/src/health/orchestrate.ts:819`) is scoped only by a **failure class** drawn from the closed set `breaker:<metric>`, `auth_permanent`, `all_streams_failed`. Against a permanent PRIMARY KEY with no TTL, written with `onConflictDoNothing`, each connection-plus-reason pair burns permanently on first use. This is **live and currently armed**: that key was dispatched and accepted for `auth_permanent` on 2026-09-01, and ADR-051b records that the recovery **rebound the same connection row with `created_at` preserved**, so the connection id is unchanged and **the next `auth_permanent` failure on the production Health connection will alert nobody**. Earlier records framed Health as the safe counter-example to Calendar; that is accurate only about the first occurrence. Re-arming both keys is Checkpoint 8.1 work. **5. ADR-034 is stale.** It states Firebase/FCM and Groq exist *"in local development only. Production has neither"*. Both were provisioned to production at Phase 3 Checkpoint 6 — production runs a `Groq Production` connection serving the `voice_transcribe` route, and the production device receives real Expo/FCM pushes. The ADR's own escape hatch (*"provisioning production is a separate, deliberate step"*) was executed; only the present-tense sentence was never updated. **6. ADR-055's Tailscale blind spot is resolved.** It required that worker-to-Tailscale-Serve reachability *"must be proven in Checkpoint 7.5"*. It was not proven in 7.5 and WAS proven in 7.7, from inside the running production worker container. Both tailnet monitor targets are now seeded and probing. **7. ADR-051's absolute is superseded.** It states *"No second development OAuth application, client, project, account or credential set exists or may be used"*. ADR-051b (owner-approved, Checkpoint 7.8B) supersedes exactly that clause for Health only: the `personal-os-health` Google Cloud project exists and is live, because the Health API rejects any token carrying scopes beyond its own. ADR-051's other clauses stand. **8. ADR-052's deployment gate is discharged.** Its `2026-09-04T20:08:25Z` milestone is `waived_by_owner` under ADR-051a, and Phase 7 deployment completed at 7.8B. **Archival guidance recorded here because a status-column sweep would get it wrong:** only **ADR-022** carries `Superseded` in the Status column, but six further ADRs are superseded IN PART by amendment rows while both remain Locked — ADR-033 by ADR-037, ADR-046 by ADR-046a, ADR-047 by ADR-047a, ADR-051 by ADR-051a and ADR-051b, ADR-052 by ADR-051a, and ADR-053 by ADR-053a. Each base ADR retains load-bearing unamended clauses, so **only ADR-022 may ever be archived wholesale**; any future archival must key off the amendment cross-references, not the Status column. **Verified accurate and needing no change** (spot-checked at 8.0): ADR-019, ADR-030, ADR-031, ADR-036, ADR-039, ADR-040, ADR-041, ADR-042, ADR-043, ADR-045, ADR-046, ADR-050, ADR-053 and ADR-053a. **Nothing was implemented to satisfy any of these corrections** — Checkpoint 8.0 is documentation only, and each remediation is assigned to a named later checkpoint (Phase 8 Checkpoint 8.0, 2026-09-02) **[Present state corrected by ADR-061, ADR-062 and ADR-065 (#3's write-side residual is closed).]**
